statement: Using the identity for $\cos 5\theta$, show that $\cos 36^{\circ}=\dfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}$.
solution: Let $c=\cos 36^{\circ}$; then $5\cdot 36^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$ so $\cos 180^{\circ}=-1=\cos 5\theta$. Using $\cos 5\theta=16\cos^{5}\theta-20\cos^{3}\theta+4\cos\theta$, we get $16c^{5}-20c^{3}+4c+1=0$. Factoring $(c+1)(16c^{4}-16c^{3}-4c^{2}+4c+1)=0$; since $c\neq -1$, the quartic gives $c=\tfrac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}$ (taking the positive root).
hints: Solve the resulting polynomial, keeping the positive root.
